families.label: Engine output
families.note: Produced by the merit-order clearing engine on the same hour's stack. Present only in the structural and hybrid models; the pure-ML model is denied these by construction so the comparison is fair.

families.label: Bid-curve shape
families.note: The aggregate supply and demand curves evaluated at a fixed price grid. These give the models the *local density* of offers around the clearing point, which is what governs how far price moves when the curve shifts - a total MW figure cannot express that.

families.label: Stack totals and counts
families.note: Scalar summaries of the hour's submitted stack.

families.label: Virtual-bid volume and distribution
families.note: Convergence-bid quantities, plus distribution statistics across pseudo-nodes. Identity-free by construction: they describe how concentrated virtual activity is, never where any individual pseudo-node sits on the real network.

families.label: Per-node history (pseudonymous)
families.note: Each node's own historical price behaviour, computed on the TRAINING MONTHS ONLY - computing them over the full year would leak the test period into the features. Keyed on the real NODE_ID from public LMP data.

families.label: System state
families.note: Cleared day-ahead schedules from CAISO's ENE_SLRS report, at ISO and TAC-zone level.

families.label: Node geography
families.note: Published coordinates where CAISO lists them.

split.note: A random split leaks: adjacent hours are highly correlated, so shuffling lets the model memorise neighbouring prices.
